catalog_quote: The only source available on Kpeen, Zwernemann (1996), is based on the brief fieldnotes prepared for publication more than 30 years after the actual fieldwork, with no original sound recordings preserved. The data are therefore to be taken with necessary reservations. Zwernemann (1996) uses only 2 tone levels for his Kpeen data. According to Zwernemann (1996:163), negation in Kpeen is marked with a morpheme nè or nì at the end of a sentence [...] (26) ná tɔ́ nè TAM know NEG 'I do not know' (Zwernemann 1996:163)

new_statements.rule_in_words: Second-hand: the only primary source (Zwernemann 1996) transcribes Kpeen with two tone levels (H marked acute, L marked grave, as in the quoted examples ná tɔ́ nè, mwɔ̀ sí à ná ná nè); Idiatov treats Kpeen as a tone language like its Samogo sisters (Dzuun, Ban 3 levels; Jo, Seen 4) but flags the two-level notation as possibly under-analysed. Nothing is said about stress or accent.
new_statements.exceptions: Idiatov notes the CFNM nì appears once with high tone in an example although low in Zwernemann's running text ('marked in the example with a high tone rather than low as in the running text'); WOCAL 2012 slide adds '(with a polar tone?)'. Reliability caveat: fieldnotes published 30+ years after fieldwork, no recordings.
new_statements.identity_note: Section 3.4 is headed 'Kpeen' and the paper identifies it as 'Kpeen (ISO 639-3: cpo)', a Samogo language of the Duun cluster; all Kpeen data are quoted from Zwernemann 1996 'Documents kpḛḛgo' p. 163, i.e. exactly Glottolog's kpee1234. Not in Glottolog's reference list for kpee1234 (Glottolog tags the paper, if at all, under other Samogo/Bobo codes); the published version is paywalled at Benjamins, the prefinal is open on the author's site (HAL halshs-01278633 has the record only).
